entries.scope_label: Corollary 2.3: general Hom-sheaf softness and restriction assertion
entries.verdict: source reading decided and retained; author claim contradicted by the recorded map
entries.printed_reading: Sous les hypothèses de (2.2), les faisceaux i_s^{-1}Hom(X,Y), Hom(X_s,Y_s) sont mous. ... Pour tout fermé A de X_s, l’application H^0(X_s,i_s^{-1}Hom(X,Y)) → H^0(A,Hom(X_s,Y_s)) déduite de (2.1.1) est surjective. Each Hom here has its printed underline.
entries.editorial_disposition: Retain the printed statement; record the separate explicit author-claim obstruction without a textual emendation.
entries.original_reason_verbatim: Take S={s}, r=∞, X=R² and Y=S¹ with their C∞ structure sheaves. Local charts of S¹ are open intervals, so §1.1 includes Y. The fibre X_s=R² is paracompact, and {s} is a paracompact fundamental neighborhood basis. Let A=S¹⊂R² and W={z:1/2<|z|<3/2}. The smooth map h:W→S¹, h(z)=z/|z|, defines a morphism of ringed spaces by pullback φ↦φ∘h and hence a section [h]_A of the printed target sheaf on closed A. Here i_s is the identity. The displayed map becomes q:C∞(R²,S¹)→H^0(A,Hom-underlined(R²,S¹)), g↦[g]_A. The sheaf definition on204 identifies its domain with all global smooth maps. A preimage g of [h]_A would satisfy g|_A=h|_A=id_{S¹}. For the inclusion i:S¹→R² this gives g∘i=id_{S¹}. On fundamental groups, i_* factors through π_1(R²)=0, since the explicit contraction H_t(z)=(1−t)z contracts R². Thus g_*∘i_*=0, whereas (id_{S¹})_*=id_Z on π_1(S¹)=Z. These two induced maps cannot agree. Consequently [h]_A has no preimage under q. See review/expose_ii/author_claim_issue_206.json for definition passages and precise scope.

entries.scope_label: Proposition 4.7(a): cohomology bound and boundedness; proof reference

entries.original_reason_verbatim: Both complete primary and native256–257 pages repeat3.5(a)’s relative-amplitude bound in4.7(a), with E2 additionally pseudo-coherent. The example S=SpecZ, X1=Y1=SpecFp, X2=Y2=S, identity f_i, E1=Fp and E2=Z/p in degree0 satisfies this added condition: [Z --p→Z] is a finite free resolution of E2. Its external tensor still identifies through pr1=id and pr2:SpecFp→SpecZ with[Fp --0→Fp] in degrees−1,0, violating the claimed[0,0] interval. A boundedness failure is explicit over A=k[ε]/(ε²): take S=SpecA, X1=Y1=Speck, X2=Y2=S, identity f_i and E1=E2=k. The two required scheme pairs have S as their second factor, so their higher Tor groups vanish. E1 is rank-one free over k and has relative perfect amplitude[0,0]. The exact free resolution ...→A --ε→A --ε→A→k has kernel=image=(ε) in each negative degree, proving that E2 is pseudo-coherent and concentrated in degree0. Definition1.6 identifies the external tensor on X=Speck with k tensor_A^L k. Tensoring that explicit resolution with k makes every differential zero, so H^j=k for every j≤0. The printed conclusion therefore fails even to give bounded cohomology. Preserve the author statement and the printed proof reference to3.5; no uniquely supported replacement hypothesis is supplied by these calculations.

entries.scope_label: 3.3.3: first category pairing and its first induced group map
entries.verdict: source reading decided and retained; author claim contradicted by the recorded tensor calculation
entries.printed_reading: Sous les hypothèses de (III 4.7), le foncteur ⊗^L_S définit des accouplements D(f1)_parf×D^b(f2)_coh→D^b(f)_coh,… qui induisent des homomorphismes K^•(f1)⊗K_•(f2)→K_•(f),…
entries.editorial_disposition: Retain the source claim in both layers; attach the explicit derived-tensor obstruction separately.
entries.original_reason_verbatim: Set A=k[ε]/(ε²), S=Spec A, X1=Y1=Spec k, X2=Y2=S, and f1,f2 equal to the respective identity maps. Both required pairs (X1,X2) and (Y1,Y2) are Tor-independent over S because Tor_i^A(k,A)=0 for i>0. Their products X and Y are Spec k and f=f1×_Sf2=id_Spec k. Take E1=k in degree0 on X1 and E2=k in degree0 on S. E1 is perfect relative to f1 with amplitude[0,0]. The free resolution P with P^n=A for n≤0 and every differential in negative degree multiplication by ε is exact in negative degrees, since ker(ε)=εA=im(ε), and H^0(P)=k. Its finite free approximations prove E2 pseudo-coherent; its own cohomology is concentrated in degree0. Thus the two input objects satisfy the printed hypotheses. In the exact construction of III1.6, pr1=id_Spec k and pr2:Spec k→Spec A, so Lpr1^*E1⊗^L_k Lpr2^*E2 = k⊗^L_k(k⊗^L_A k). The resolution identifies this with k⊗_A P, whose differentials are all zero and whose term in every degree n≤0 is k. Hence H^n=k for every n≤0. The inclusion J:D^b(k)_coh→D^−(k)_coh sends a bounded object to a complex with vanishing cohomology in all sufficiently negative degrees, so the displayed tensor object is not isomorphic to an object in its essential image. The advertised first pairing therefore does not land in D^b(f)_coh, and cannot induce the first stated Grothendieck homomorphism by the displayed tensor functor. The printed text is retained; no replacement theorem or assertion about all abstract group pairings is made. See author_claim_issue_295.json.
